A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Weaver. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including the additional Appendices F and G in v2.

before.justification: v1 reports original QA accuracy, efficiency measurements, optimization and error analyses, and a BIRD evaluation in Appendix E.1.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and explicitly reports preliminary HiTab testing in Appendix G.

M1.justification: The preprocessing, planning, verification, SQL/LLM execution, answer extraction, and optimization procedures are retained. Expanded execution and batching descriptions explain mechanisms already represented in v1's prompts and appendix; they do not establish an algorithm change.

E1.justification: Appendix G newly reports preliminary testing on hierarchical HiTab tables; v1 discusses HiTab's characteristics and possible adaptation without explicitly reporting such testing. The existing hybrid, multimodal, and BIRD coverage remains. OTT-QA is retained in the multimodal evaluation.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the corresponding accuracy, efficiency, and error comparisons. Chain-of-Table and TAG receive additional discussion in Appendix F but are not newly evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The newly reported HiTab pilot uses schema flattening and normalization before SQL execution. Existing evaluation procedures are otherwise retained. The BIRD sample specification, temperature, and REM implementation details are new disclosures, without evidence that existing experiments were reconfigured or rerun.

E4.justification: Section 3.2 removes the qualitative diagnosis that BlendSQL frequently encounters type errors when integrating LLM outputs into SQL. The large-table analysis, optimization study, SQL/planning error comparison, plan-verification ablation, and appendix execution examples remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports independent repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. Baseline self-consistency annotations remain unchanged. Disclosing the fixed temperature does not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 1–8 retain their numerical values. v2 adds the qualitative HiTab SQL-execution outcome and removes the BlendSQL type-error observation. The BIRD accuracy remains 91%, now explicitly attributed to 30 curated development queries; this is not a performance gain.

T1.justification: Neither version develops formal theorems or proofs. The operational definitions of hybrid queries and REM are retained. The added columns-times-rows batching explanation supplies implementation detail rather than a new theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the claims of flexible SQL/LLM planning, improved accuracy, efficiency, and interpretability. Replacing 'semi-structured tables' with tables containing embedded unstructured text clarifies the meaning already specified in v1's Appendix D.

C2.justification: Appendix G explicitly interprets preliminary testing as supporting hierarchical and multi-table applicability when semantic inference is unnecessary, and describes schema-aware and multilingual extensions. This adds qualifications to the existing applicability discussion, although the original limitations paragraph remains unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplements the extensive existing prompt appendix with the REM answer-formatting prompt and a code/scripts link. It also specifies temperature 0.01, reuse of the same LLM across stages, batching rules, random sampling for the optimization study, and the 30-query BIRD development subset.

R1.justification: New Appendix F contrasts Weaver with Chain-of-Table and explains the baseline-selection rationale concerning ReAcTable and TAG. References are added for Spider, HiTab, BIRD, and MMTBench, and Tan et al. replaces Rajkumar et al. for Text-to-SQL. Most other bibliography changes update existing works.

P1.justification: v2 edits terminology and sentences, expands REM and execution explanations, separates baseline descriptions, and adds short related-method and future-work appendices. The main section order and overall narrative remain substantially intact.

P2.justification: All eight figures and eight tables are retained, with unchanged figure artwork. Captions are clarified, Table 2 explicitly labels hybrid subsets, model-name footnotes are added, and figures, tables, and the author block are repositioned or reformatted.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by identifying the small curated sample behind the BIRD result and documenting REM normalization, execution settings, and code access. Clearer labels and explanations also help readers assess the work. The main empirical evidence remains unchanged, and the HiTab pilot lacks sample counts and accuracy, so the overall improvement is limited.
